headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad write/network autonomy can conflict with ctx’s filesystem/MCP observation and create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code post-tool events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem access, while Devin acts autonomously in a cloud workspace with MCP and broad APIs. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Devin writes attacker-controlled text into shared artifacts that ctx parses. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF Devin writes untrusted text into files or tickets that ctx later parses as instructions
IF ctx consumes Claude Code tool output or workspace files without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict ctx to read-only observation of designated paths
Add provenance tags to all Devin-written artifacts
Disable automatic instruction parsing from workspace text
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and external services, and Devin explicitly handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens. ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers. If they share a workspace or integration surface, sensitive material can flow from ctx into Devin’s broader networked environment. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style setups, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF ctx and Devin share a filesystem, repo clone, or MCP server
IF sensitive logs, graph data, or secrets are present in that shared surface
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Remove secrets from shared directories
Limit Devin’s access to only required repos
Rotate any exposed integration tokens
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, and broad network egress; ctx also has filesystem access and can install packages and run browsers. If both operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt state. Because neither profile shows locking or coordination, the unsafe default is credible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or filesystem path
IF Devin and ctx can modify git state or files concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or repos
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent
Run one agent in read-only mode
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and Devin is a long-running planner-executor that can act autonomously. If ctx’s outputs are treated as authoritative by Devin, or Devin’s generated facts are fed back into ctx without verification, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or other actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF Devin consumes ctx-generated summaries as ground truth
IF ctx-derived facts are used to trigger GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, or Notion actions
mitigations: Require human review before actions
Add a verification step against source artifacts
Mark ctx output as advisory only
Disable auto-commit or auto-ticket creation
requires-engineering: implement confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Devin’s docs show Slack, Jira, Linear, Notion, GitHub, and integration-token handling, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records. If regulated or sensitive data is present in ctx artifacts, Devin’s broader SaaS integrations can create retention and residency mismatches. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency boundary, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ctx artifacts contain regulated data or customer secrets
IF Devin syncs those artifacts into Slack, Jira, Linear, Notion, or GitHub
mitigations: Block regulated data from shared workflows
Redact logs before handoff
Limit Devin integrations to non-sensitive projects
Set retention rules for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: document residency and DPA boundaries
